name: Quest Dialogue Loop
description: A reusable RPG narrative loop: branching dialogue offers and advances staged quests; combat, inventory, world flags, and explicit objective credits advance only Quest Log; completion enters an exactly-once mixed-reward coordinator; XP, currency, and inventory own their own grants; HUD and journal projections update without gaining authority; completed narrative changes trigger persistence. Attribute checks and condition reads are synchronous queries, not event round trips. Legacy flat quests and inline rewards remain available outside coordinated mode.

components.role: conversation rendering and raw choice intentions
conditional traversal, once-only choices, synchronous checks, and consequence requests
synchronous deterministic attribute checks and restorable roll cursor
persistent world consequences and synchronous flag-condition reads
eligible enemy-defeat facts for staged objectives
item-reward ownership and item-added objective facts
sole authority for quest acceptance, staged objectives, transitions, completion, and failure
stable grant ids, restored deduplication, and one mixed-reward emission per completion
XP grant ownership and level growth
safe layout metrics for the removable tracker
filterable active, completed, and failed quest read model
clue and lore entries requested by dialogue consequences
durable snapshots after completed quest, dialogue, flag, journal, and reward changes

connections.note: Defeats are objective facts; combat never completes a quest directly.
Collection objectives observe the existing inventory owner.
Ordered failure or branch conditions reevaluate on relevant world changes.
The renderer reports a choice; the engine interprets it.
Dialogue requests a world consequence without owning flag state.
Offers, acceptance, objective credits, advances, failures, and turn-ins enter only Quest Log.
Narrative Journal records clues, not quest completion.
Coordinated mode carries a stable completionId and rewards bundle with no inline payout.
XP consumes only xp entries from the mixed grant.
Currency consumes only currency entries from the mixed grant.
Inventory consumes only item entries from the mixed grant.

acceptanceCriteria: Legacy flat quests retain inlineLegacy payout by default, and legacy dialogue choices without extended fields retain their existing traversal behavior.
Staged quests enforce prerequisites and ordered transitions; required objectives advance stages while optional objectives never block them.
Objective dedupe keys and stable completion ids prevent repeated combat, inventory, or dialogue facts from producing duplicate progress or completion.
Failure and completion terminals settle exactly once, and no terminal stage can continue transitioning afterward.
Dialogue conditions query quest, flag, and attribute owners; unavailable choices neither traverse nor emit consequences.
Attribute checks execute synchronously through Attribute Sheet, and the same seed, restored check cursor, attributes, difficulties, and choice sequence reproduce their results.
A once-only dialogue choice restored in resolvedChoiceIds cannot emit its quest, flag, or journal consequences again.
Dialogue Tree Engine emits consequence requests but never directly changes quest state, world flags, journal entries, XP, currency, or inventory.
Quest Tracker, Quest Journal, and Narrative Journal are read-only projections; removing any or all of them does not change quest progression or rewards.
Coordinated quest completion suppresses inline questRewarded and emits one stable completion bundle to Quest Reward Coordinator.
A duplicate or restored completionId produces no second rewardGranted event, while malformed bundles are rejected before entering the ledger.
A mixed reward reaches XP, Currency, and Core Inventory through their existing reward sinks, with each owner consuming only its declared grant kinds.
Quest state, dialogue positions, world flags, objective dedupe keys, reward ledger ids, and attribute check cursor restore through their respective owners without replaying completed side effects.
Rejected dialogue choices, unavailable quest actions, duplicate completions, and malformed rewards do not trigger successful-change persistence events.
Safe Area Layout and Quest Tracker can be removed without affecting the dialogue-to-quest-to-reward core; combat and inventory objective sources are optional when a quest does not use them.
Content validation rejects unknown quest actions, bad credit targets, dangling dialogue destinations, quest-stage cycles, unreachable quest stages, and missing completion terminals before runtime.
The pack contains original generic contracts and examples only; it supplies no commercial writing, characters, quests, items, or exact balance tables and implies no runtime adapter implementation.
